Article Text:

What happened on Tuesday

NEW DELHI: A day after INDIA bloc MPs marched towards the Election Commission and Rahul Gandhi staged an hours-long sit-in, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge is set to host opposition MPs for lunch in Delhi.Kharge has invited INDIA bloc MPs for lunch at 1.30 pm at Sagar Ratna on Janpath, sources informed ANI. The MPs are also expected to sign a letter seeking a meeting with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The meeting comes after a dramatic day of protests on Tuesday, when opposition MPs marched from Parliament towards the Election Commission headquarters, demanding a meeting with the election commissioners over their allegations of irregularities in the electoral process.The march was stopped by Delhi Police near Akashvani Bhawan, after which opposition MPs staged a sit-in. Rahul Gandhi, along with Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other Congress leaders, had entered the Akashvani Bhawan premises and insisted that the delegation be allowed to meet the election commissioners.The protest continued for nearly nine hours before police detained several opposition MPs and took them to New Police Lines at Kingsway Camp.Around 50 MPs were detained, while police figures put the total number of people detained at around 260.Rahul Gandhi questioned why elected representatives were being prevented from meeting the Election Commission when its office was only metres away. “If the representatives of the people cannot meet the Election Commission, then what is the meaning of democracy?” he said.After his release, Congress MP Pawan Khera warned that Tuesday’s protest was not the end of the opposition campaign against the CEC.“If Gyanesh Kumar thinks that just because we went home today, it is all over, he needs to understand that this is merely the beginning — nothing has ended yet,” Khera said.The lunch hosted by Kharge is therefore expected to serve as a meeting point for the alliance to discuss its immediate strategy and decide how to sustain pressure over the “vote chori” issue.The opposition has been demanding Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and is seeking a meeting with the election commissioners to press its allegations. The Election Commission has maintained its position on the issues raised by the opposition.
Article Summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge is set to host opposition MPs for lunch in Delhi. The MPs are also expected to sign a letter seeking a meeting with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The meeting comes after a dramatic day of protests on Tuesday, when opposition MPs marched towards the Election Commission headquarters.

Article Title: Three new SC judges take oath, all in the name of God; number of women judges in SC – three out of 37
Article Text:
CJI Surya Kant administered oath to Justices Agarwal, Upadhyaya and Singh

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Three new Supreme Court Judges – Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh – on Tuesday took oath of office in the name of God taking the working strength of SC to 37 judges, just one short of the sanctioned strength.CJI Surya Kant administered oath to Justices Agarwal, Upadhyaya and Singh, who were chief justices of Gujarat, Delhi and Telangana HCs respectively, in the presence of SC judges, attorney general R Venkataramani, solicitor general Tushar Mehta and other senior advocates and lawyers.With the elevation of Justice Agarwal, who is the 13th women judge of SC, the strength of women judges in the apex court at present became three. The other two being Justices B V Nagarathna, who is scheduled to become the first woman CJI on Sep 24 next year, and Justice V Mohana.During the tenure of Justice N V Ramana as CJI, the Supreme Court had the highest number of sitting SC judges at four – Justices India Banerjee, Nagarathna, Hima Kohli and Bela M Trivedi, last three of whom had taken oath on Aug 31, 2021. While the Collegium led by Justice Ramana had recommended appointment of three women judges, the present collegium led by CJI Kant has so far appointed two women judges.SC got its first woman judge in M Fathima Beevi on Oct 6, 1989, 39 years after SC was established. Justice Beevi had retired from Kerala HC on Apr 29, 1989, but was elevated to the SC five months after retirement. Other women judges in SC were – Justices Sujata V Manohar, Ruma Pal, Gyan Sudha Misra, Ranjana P Desai, R Bhanumathi and Indu Malhotra.SC judge strength was increased from 34 to 38, including the CJI, initially through an Ordinance on May 16. The corresponding Amendment Act was passed by Parliament which received the President's assent on Aug 11. In Aug 2019, during the tenure of CJI Ranjan Gogoi, the sanctioned strength of SC judges was increased from 31 to 34, including CJI.The SC had started in 1950 with a sanctioned strength of 8 Judges, which was increased to 11 in 1956, 14 in 1960, 18 in 1978, 26 in 1986, and 31 in 2009. SC as of Tuesday has a pendency of 95, 481 cases.
Article Summary: Three new Supreme Court Judges – Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh – on Tuesday took oath of office in the name of God. The working strength of SC to 37 judges, just one short of the sanctioned strength.

Article Title: 'Beyond limits': Ex-CJI Gavai, former judges slam SC judge Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks amid EC-SIR row
Article Text:
What Bhuyan had said

NEW DELHI: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai and other retired judges on Monday condemned Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks on the Election Commission.Gavai said that a sitting judge should not have made comments on the ongoing row over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls as the matter is sub judice before the top court."Judicial propriety would not permit him to make any comment on the matter which is sub judice before the court," Gavai told news agency PTI.Retired Delhi high court judges SN Dhingra and RS Sodhi also questioned Bhuyan's remarks.Justice Dhingra said Bhuyan's statement was "way beyond the limits of a sitting top court judge" and such comments should not be made at a public event when the issue is pending before the same court."He should have thought a thousand times before making such a statement," Dhingra said, adding that Justice Bhuyan did not know the full facts of the issue.Justice R S Sodhi also criticised Justice Bhuyan for calling the SIR exercise disenfranchisement and said that the right to vote was governed by the statutory framework."Whether you have a vote or you don't have a vote depends upon the statute. If you fall within the parameters of the statute, you have a vote.If you don't fall within the parameters of the statute, you don't have a vote," Justice Sodhi said."I mean, these hardline thinking and these hardline statements, to my mind, are not a very mature way of looking at a thing, especially when you are supposed to be in a field which is supposed to be excellent in its rationalising," he said.This comes a day after Justice Bhuyan said that any process that "disenfranchises" millions of Indian citizens was "intrinsically arbitrary" and a "negation" of the constitutional order.While delivering the valedictory address at the 19th Justice Bodh Raj Sawhney Memorial Moot Court Competition at NALSAR University of Law on Sunday, Justice Bhuyan said that the Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens, one with voting rights and the other without voting rights, and no amount of "whataboutery" could justify such a process.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary. No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution and I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution of India,” Bar and Bench quoted Justice Bhuyan as saying.He said the Constitution does not create two classes of citizens based on voting rights and added that wholesale disenfranchisement would violate Articles 326 and 14.“No authority can do it; no court can condone it. No one is above the Constitution,” he said.This is not the first time that Justice Bhuyan has put forth his views on issues being discussed in the public domain.Recently, NALSAR Hyderabad was in the news after a section of its students wrote to the vice chancellor, registrar and professors of the institution, opposing any proposal to invite Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as chief guest to the varsity's convocation.Justice Bhuyan, who served as the Chancellor of NALSAR, on Sunday said he can be legitimately proud of the students of the institution."You have shown to the country and the world what a university student, that too, a student of law, should be like. You are brilliant. You are bold and you are brave," he said.
Article Summary: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai and other retired judges on Monday condemned Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks on the Election Commission. Justice Dhingra and RS Sodhi said Bhuya's statement was "way beyond the limits of a sitting top court judge" This comes a day after Justice Bhuayan said that any process that "disenfranchises" millions of Indian citizens was "intrinsically arbitrary"

Article Title: Supreme Court to examine plea seeking recall of split verdict on CEC, EC appointment law
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to examine a plea seeking recall of its September 23 split verdict on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the chief election commissioner (CEC) and election commissioners (ECs) should be heard by a five-judge Bench.Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the petitioners, mentioned the plea before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and sought its listing. “We will examine and take a call,” the CJI said.The split verdict was delivered by Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma. Justice Datta held that a two-judge Bench could hear the challenge and opposed referring it to a larger Bench, while Justice Sharma favoured a five-judge Bench.With the two judges differing on the issue, the matter was referred to the CJI for constitution of an appropriate Bench.The top court's agreement came a day after massive protest by Rahul Gandhi-led opposition demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over poll body's special intensive revision exercise.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to examine a plea seeking recall of its September 23 split verdict. The split verdict was delivered by Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma. Justice Datta held that a two-judge Bench could hear the challenge and opposed referring it to a larger Bench.

Article Title: 'Making steady progress, regaining health': Indian embassy in UAE updates on flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar
Article Text:
Capt. Smit Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot, an Omani national with a crash axe.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Captain Smit Machchhar is “making steady progress” and “regaining his health” after being seriously injured in an attack by his co-pilot on a flydubai flight last week, the Indian Embassy in the UAE said on Tuesday.Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot, an Omani national with a crash axe, an emergency tool typically kept in the cockpit during flydubai flight FZ1073 on Wednesday. The motive for the attack remains unclear.“Capt Smit continues to make steady progress and is regaining his health. The Embassy remains in close touch with his family, doctors & local authorities, extending all possible assistance,” the embassy said in a post on X.“We thank everyone for their prayers & wish him a speedy recovery,” it added.The flight, carrying 174 passengers, sent emergency signals after the attack and rapidly descended more than 17,000 feet from an altitude of 34,000 feet.Machchhar, who was lying injured on the cockpit floor, realised that the aircraft was descending and made “one last push” to open the cockpit door.He managed to activate the door release despite being seriously injured and covered in blood.Two reserve pilots then took control of the aircraft and landed it safely at Prince Sultan Bin Abdulaziz Airport in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The co-pilot was taken into custody, while Machchhar was taken to a nearby hospital for treatment.Machchhar was initially admitted to a hospital in Tabuk before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi for further medical treatment, PTI reported.On October 1, India's ambassador to the UAE, Deepak Mittal, had said Machchhar was “in good health and recovering well”. Mittal had also visited the injured captain and his family at the hospital.The investigation into the attack is ongoing, with the motive behind the co-pilot's actions still unclear.
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar was seriously injured in an attack by his co-pilot on a flydubai flight last week. He was attacked by the Omani national with a crash axe, an emergency tool typically kept in the cockpit. The motive for the attack remains unclear.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court of India Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan (PTI Photo)

-

Detaching right to vote from citizen is like taking soul out of body: Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad. “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

Article Title: Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation makes a new move amid financial controversy as Ed and Donna Kelce enter the picture
Article Text:
Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation makes a new move amid financial controversy as Ed and Donna Kelce enter the picture (Image via Getty: Ed Kelce, Travis Kelce, and Donna Kelce)

Travis Kelce’s foundation continues youth work amid financial scrutiny

Donna Kelce joins students for special Chiefs experience

Ed Kelce connects family legacy with children

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Founded by Travis Kelce in 2015, 87 & Running Foundation aims to empower underserved youth by providing resources and opportunities in education, athletics, STEM, and the arts. Its “Ignition Lab” collaboration with the nonprofit organization Operation Breaththrough reflects the foundation’s mission.Through the Ignition Lab program, under-resourced teenagers from Kansas City neighborhoods can explore STEM and entrepreneurship with mentorship, equipment, and hands-on learning.Although 87 & Running Foundation’s Instagram account has seen no recent activity, its charitable work continues through initiatives like Operation Breakthrough’s Ignition Lab.According to the foundation’s website, the Ignition Lab program serves about 700 students daily. Young people have opportunities to learn, create, develop practical skills, and explore several pathways that could shape their future education and careers.87 & Running Foundation’s official Instagram account has not posted any content since January 2026. At the same time, social media fans raised money-laundering allegations against the foundation.According to The Arizona Republic, the foundation’s IRS filings reported raising about $1.5 million and spending roughly $1.1 million over a multi-year period [2021 to 2024].Only 41 cents of every dollar was reportedly directed to charitable programs.CharityWatch executive director, Laurie Styron, told The Arizona Republic that, “players and their managers need to stop using charities this way. Don’t get creative. Don’t look for loopholes.If you establish a charity, stop mixing in business interests or using friends to operate it. Do it the right way or don’t do it at all. There are a lot of ways for players to give back without founding their own charity.”Despite this growing tension, Travis Kelce’s foundation reportedly continued its work through the Ignition Lab program with Operation Breakthrough. Operation Breakthrough is a nonprofit organization that provides educational and developmental opportunities for children and families in Kansas City.Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation funds and powers its Ignition Lab program. The program gives 14- to 18-year-old teenagers access to resources that promote innovation, technical learning, and entrepreneurial thinking. This partnership expands 87 & Running Foundation’s financial support to create opportunities for young people.In August 2026, Operation Breakthrough expressed heartfelt gratitude to Travis Kelce for arranging an opportunity for Ignition Lab students. The students attended the Kansas City Chiefs’ first preseason game from Kelce’s suite at Arrowhead Stadium.The organization wrote on Instagram, “Talk about a suit surprise! Thanks to Travis Kelce, our Ignition Lab students experienced the Chiefs’ first preseason game from his suite at Arrowhead!”The post also mentioned that the students met Travis Kelce’s mother, Donna Kelce, during the outing. This experience gave participating students a heartfelt opportunity to enjoy a Chiefs game. It also helped them create lasting memories connected to their Kansas City community.The 87 & Running Foundation’s 2025 annual report speaks for the foundation’s continued charitable work.Their website also provides information about its programs and partnerships. However, their collaboration with Operation Breakthrough through Ignition Lat provides additional insight into the foundation's activities and its connection to the Kelce family. In particular, Travis Kelce’s father, Ed Kelce.On September 17, 2026, Operation Breakthrough shared a post on Instagram about Ed Kelce visiting. The father of NFL legends Jason and Travis Kelce read to first-grade students and showed them the cutest, rarest childhood photos of Jason and Travis.The organization wrote, “Storytime with a side of Kelce family throwbacks! Ed Kelce stopped by to read to our first graders, then gave them a peek at Travis and Jason when they were little, just like them! Thank you, Ed, for sharing your time and a little family history with our children!”Yesterday, it was Travis Kelce’s 37th birthday on October 5, 2026. The little angels at Operation Breakthrough sent warmest wishes for the Kansas City Chiefs tight end through an adorable Instagram reel.The organization collaborated on the post with 87 & Running Foundation and called it, “Little voices, BIG birthday wishes! Happy birthday, Travis! Sending lots of love from all of us at Operation Breakthrough.” This post marks the 87 & Running Foundation’s first social media update since January 2026.
Article Summary: 87 & Running Foundation aims to empower underserved youth by providing resources and opportunities in education, athletics, STEM, and the arts. Its “Ignition Lab” collaboration with the nonprofit organization Operation Breaththrough reflects the foundation’s mission.Through the Ignition Lab program, under- resourced teenagers from Kansas City neighborhoods can explore STEM and entrepreneurship.

Article Title: Travis and Jason Kelce quietly donated $10,000 to help turn a $50,000 Olympic fundraiser into a family reunion in Milan
Article Text:
Travis and Jason Kelce (Instagram)

Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce helped Laila Edwards’ family reach Milan

Travis Kelce supported Laila Edwards before Olympic gold

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Earlier this year, Travis and Jason Kelce made a quiet contribution that helped make a special Olympic moment possible for U.S. hockey star Laila Edwards. The brothers donated $10,000 to a fundraiser that helped bring Edwards’ family and friends to Milan for the 2026 Winter Olympics. Their support came after her family faced a difficult choice between watching her Olympic debut and covering everyday household expenses. Edwards went on to help Team USA win gold, creating a moment her family could celebrate together.Edwards’ Olympic journey was already historic before she stepped onto the ice. The 22-year-old became the first Black American to win an Olympic medal in women’s ice hockey after Team USA defeated Canada in the gold-medal game.But getting her loved ones to Italy was not easy.Edwards’ father, Robert Edwards, launched a GoFundMe campaign titled “Send Laila’s Family to the Olympics to Cheer Her On!” with a $50,000 target. The goal was designed to help the family avoid choosing between Olympic travel and essential bills at home in Cleveland Heights, Ohio.The Kelce brothers, who also grew up in Cleveland Heights, had followed Edwards’ career since she became the first Black player to make the U.S.senior women’s national team in 2023. They later supported her through an anonymous $10,000 donation.The contribution helped make the trip possible for 14 people, including Edwards’ parents, grandmother, aunt, cousin and older brother.The family had initially been able to afford travel for only two people.“We had to start talking about how to get money,” her mother Charone Gray-Edwards said, according to the Associated Press. “Who would go? How would we afford it?”The Chiefs tight end’s support extended beyond the financial contribution. Travis also reached out to Edwards before her Olympic debut, offering encouragement as she prepared for the biggest stage of her young career.“He was just saying, everyone’s got my back. He’s rooting for me,” she said, per the AP. “They didn’t have to do that, but they did. And I’m really grateful.”Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie, were also in the stands for the gold-medal game, giving Edwards a familiar connection to her hometown while she represented the United States.Edwards made an impact on the ice, recording an assist during the gold-medal victory. Team USA eventually defeated Canada 2-1 in overtime, securing only the third Olympic gold medal in U.S. women’s hockey history.For Edwards, the victory was more than a sporting achievement. Her family had made the long journey to Milan, and the Kelce brothers had quietly helped make that possible. Their involvement added another meaningful layer to an already historic Olympic chapter.
Article Summary: Travis and Jason Kelce donated $10,000 to a fundraiser that helped bring Laila Edwards' family and friends to Milan for the 2026 Winter Olympics. Edwards went on to help Team USA win gold, creating a moment her family could celebrate together.

Article Title: “Not have been able to go without his help”: How Conor McGregor turned from a hero into a helping hand for two 13-year-old fans with a €10,000 heartwarming move
Article Text:
How Conor McGregor turned from a hero into a helping hand for two 13-year-old fans(Getty Images)

Conor McGregor gave the twins €10,000 when they needed it most

The €10,000 gift became bigger than one trip

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Adam and Dylan Duffy, Conor McGregor had always been the fighter they looked up to. The Ballycanew twins had started their own MMA journey and dreamed of competing on a bigger stage. Then, in June 2022, McGregor noticed their fundraiser and stepped in with €10,000. The donation did more than help two young fighters reach Abu Dhabi. It gave them a moment they never expected from the man they had followed for years.Adam and Dylan had earned places on the Irish MMA Youth International Team and were preparing for the IMMAF Youth World Championships in Abu Dhabi in 2022. But getting there came with a cost. The twins launched a fundraiser with a target of around €6,000 to cover their trip.Their mother, Liz Duffy, also tried to spread the word online. She tagged McGregor in social media posts and hoped he might share the boys' story. Instead, the former UFC champion did something much bigger.In June 2022, McGregor donated €10,000 to the fundraiser. He then commented online: “Done! Do the land proud I know.” The donation pushed the twins beyond their original target and gave them the financial support they needed for the trip.The reaction from Adam showed just how much the moment meant to them. Speaking to the Gorey Guardian in June 2022 after learning about the donation, Adam said he was at training when his coach told him about it.Surprisingly, Adam initially thought his coach was joking until he saw McGregor’s comment himself. He even joked that he now felt he had to win because McGregor had donated the money.“I was going insane!I thought he was joking until he showed me the comments. I feel like I have to win now because he donated all that money.’ Adam said.Dylan also understood how important the donation could be. Speaking to the Gorey Guardian in June 2022, he said the brothers might not have been able to make the trip without McGregor’s help.He said, “We might not have been able to go without his help. There are so many gyms out there and he donated to us, which is insane.”That made the gesture more personal. The twins had spent years watching McGregor compete. Now, the UFC star had helped them take the next step in their own MMA careers.The twins did not stop fundraising after McGregor's donation. Adam and Dylan, along with their parents Jason and Liz, planned to use extra funds to buy equipment for their coach Richie Ivory’s gym and help other Irish fighters travel to the IMMAF World Championships. They also planned to support the Waterford Neonatal Unit, where the twins were born.The brothers had already spent four years training with Ivory before the 2022 championship opportunity. They first joined his jiu-jitsu classes after he returned to Ireland from Australia. Their training later moved toward MMA, where both boys developed a strong interest in the sport.McGregor’s €10,000 donation therefore did not simply cover a plane ticket. It helped two young Irish fighters chase a dream they had worked toward for years.For Adam and Dylan, there was also a personal reward. After receiving the donation, they hoped to meet McGregor at his pub and thank him themselves. Adam even joked, “I’m basically friends with Conor now!"For two 13-year-old fighters who had grown up admiring McGregor, getting help from their hero was already an unforgettable chapter. The fact that his €10,000 gift could also help other young Irish fighters made the story even bigger.
Article Summary: Adam and Dylan Duffy had earned places on the Irish MMA Youth International Team. They were preparing for the IMMAF Youth World Championships in Abu Dhabi in 2022. The twins launched a fundraiser with a target of around €6,000 to cover their trip. Conor McGregor noticed their fundraiser and stepped in with €10,000.

Messi on the scoresheet

NEW DELHI: Lionel Messi ’s final appearance for Argentina ended with victory, emotion and one last unforgettable night at the Monumental as the South American side defeated Benin 3-0 on Wednesday.The occasion was as much about Messi as the result. The stadium was packed long before kick-off, with the Argentine captain receiving an extraordinary farewell.Fabio Santana, a Malvinas War veteran and singer, performed the Argentine national anthem as Messi stood alongside his children, visibly emotional. A giant Messi shirt covered the pitch before the crowd erupted into a rendition of “Muchachos”.At the 10-minute mark, the match paused for another tribute, with every Benin player taking the opportunity to shake Messi’s hand.Argentina dominated possession early and repeatedly tried to find their captain in dangerous positions. Messi came close with a free-kick from outside the box, but Benin’s goalkeeper made a fine save.Lautaro Martínez also threatened after a run into the area, while another Messi pass nearly released him into space. Benin, however, refused to sit back completely and gradually grew into the contest.They eventually switched to a back five, with Messi receiving close attention whenever he came near the penalty area.As it happened: Argentina vs Benin Highlights The breakthrough finally arrived shortly after half-time. Julián Álvarez won a corner after bursting down the left, and Messi delivered the set-piece perfectly.Nicolás Otamendi, left completely unmarked, volleyed home to put Argentina ahead. It was a fitting goal for the veteran defender, who was also making his final appearance for the national team.Argentina doubled their advantage through Nico Paz. The youngster, who had just come onto the pitch as a substitute, collected the ball and produced a beautiful left-footed curling finish, drawing comparisons with Messi’s trademark style.Messi was involved again, providing the assist as Paz announced himself on the biggest stage.Then came the moment everyone inside the Monumental had been waiting for. Messi stepped up from the penalty spot and calmly sent the goalkeeper the wrong way, placing the ball into the top-right corner for 3-0.There was still time for one final glimpse of magic. Messi had a late effort saved before another strike hit the post, and in the dying seconds he won a free-kick in his familiar range. He took responsibility one last time, but the effort sailed over the crossbar.The whistle confirmed Argentina’s 3-0 victory. For Messi, though, the scoreline was almost secondary. The night belonged to the boy from Rosario who became Argentina’s greatest footballer, and who finally said goodbye to the shirt he made his own.
Article Summary: Argentina defeated Benin 3-0 in Lionel Messi's final appearance for the national team. Messi was given an emotional farewell before kick-off at the Monumental in New Delhi. Julián Álvarez, Nicolás Otamendi, Nico Paz and Messi scored for Argentina.

NEW DELHI: India captain Shreyas Iyer has made a stunning leap into the top 10 of the ICC T20I batting rankings after his breathtaking maiden century, while Axar Patel has also broken into the elite list following a dramatic rise in the latest update.Iyer has jumped 18 places to seventh in the T20I batting rankings after smashing an unbeaten 102 off just 43 balls in India's series opener against the West Indies in Lucknow. The century, the first of his T20I career, has propelled the India skipper into the top 10 for the first time.The 31-year-old's explosive knock has also strengthened India's presence at the top end of the shortest-format batting rankings. India now have four players inside the top 10, with Ishan Kishan at No. 1, Abhishek Sharma at No. 2, Iyer at No. 7 and Tilak Varma at No. 10.Iyer's rise is among the biggest movements in the latest rankings and comes after an innings that underlined his ability to dominate an international attack from the outset.Iyer is not the only Indian making a major move in the latest rankings. All-rounder Axar Patel has climbed 16 places to seventh among T20I bowlers, joining the top 10 after a strong week for India's spin department.There has also been a major change at the very top of the bowling rankings. Afghanistan's Rashid Khan has reclaimed the No. 1 spot, replacing Pakistan's Abrar Ahmed.Bangladesh's Nasum Ahmed has climbed three places to eighth, while teammate Mahedi Hasan has made an even bigger jump, moving up 10 spots to ninth. Article Title: ‘When are you going to play him?’: Ex-India batter questions decision to bench Nitish Reddy
Article Text:
India's Nitish Kumar Reddy (PTI Photo)

Chopra unhappy with West Indies batting

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India opener Aakash Chopra believes the team management’s selection thinking does not currently match his own, questioning the decision to leave out Nitish Kumar Reddy from the first T20I against the West Indies in Lucknow.India began the five-match series with an eight-wicket win on Tuesday after bowling out the West Indies for 171 and chasing down the target with 32 balls to spare.While Chopra felt Reddy should have featured in the series opener, he also praised Naman Dhir for making a strong impact after being trusted with the ball.“The spinners took eight (seven) wickets. Personally, I would put my hand up. I thought Nitish Kumar Reddy should have been played. If you are not going to play Nitish now, when are you going to play him? My thinking and the Indian team's alignment are not sitting together,” he said in a video shared on his YouTube channel, 'Aakash Chopra.'Dhir justified the faith shown in him by returning figures of 3/31 from his four overs. His three wickets came immediately after he had been hit for a six, with Shai Hope, Romario Shepherd and Shamar Springer all dismissed following maximums off the previous delivery.Chopra was particularly impressed by the way Dhir adjusted his bowling and responded to the pressure.“However, there is one thing for sure. This team has great confidence in Naman Dhir. They feel this guy has a huge upside, which is correct. He bats very well, and they are repeatedly making him bowl along with that. Only five bowlers were used, and he picked up three wickets, where he also applied his brain,” the cricketer-turned-commentator observed.“He got hit for a six and bowled the next ball slightly far and slow. Then he bowled a slightly flat and full ball to Romario Shepherd on his legs and got hit for a six. He got the next ball to drift away with a round arm. That tells you that the guy is thinking and is executing that skill after that. The seam position was good. So, a lot of things were super impressive about Naman Dhir,” he added.Dhir removed Hope after the West Indies batter made 52 off 37 balls, before dismissing Shepherd for 7 off 5 and Springer for 9 off 7.Chopra also criticised the West Indies for failing to make the most of the conditions, arguing that the hosts should have been chasing a much higher total.He praised Kuldeep Yadav , who took 2/33 in four overs, and Axar Patel , who returned 2/26 from 3.1 overs, but felt the West Indies batting unit failed to capitalise.“Kuldeep Yadav picked up two wickets. Axar Patel bowled the sixth over as a maiden and picked up Rovman Powell's wicket in that. West Indies, you didn't bat well. This was a pitch on which 200 should have been scored easily. Your batting was extremely ordinary, and you reached 170,” he said.Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford were the only West Indies batters to make substantial contributions, with Hope scoring 52 and Rutherford hitting 56 off 34 balls.Chopra also pointed to Mayank Yadav's performance as an area of concern. The fast bowler, returning from injury, finished with 1/40 from his four overs and appeared to rely heavily on slower deliveries.“You left a lot on the pitch. Hope scored a fifty and another fifty by Sherfane Rutherford, but what happened in the middle was avoidable. Mayank Yadav was slightly expensive. It felt like he was slightly rusty, as he is returning from injury and hasn't played a lot of cricket,” Chopra observed.Only Akeal Hosein, who made 15 off 9, and Kamil Pooran, with 12 off 11, joined Hope and Rutherford in reaching double figures for the West Indies.India's bowlers ultimately kept the visitors to 171 before Shreyas Iyer's unbeaten 102 off 43 balls powered the hosts to a comfortable victory and a 1-0 series lead.
Article Summary: India beat the West Indies by eight wickets in the first T20I in Lucknow. Aakash Chopra questioned the decision to leave out Nitish Kumar Reddy. He praised Naman Dhir for making a strong impact after being trusted with the ball.

NEW DELHI: Captain Shreyas Iyer created a new record for India in T20I cricket after scoring a stunning unbeaten century against the West Indies in Lucknow on Tuesday evening. With the score, he surpassed one record held by legendary Virat Kohli.Batting at No. 4, the Indian captain smashed 102 not out from just 43 balls, hitting 10 fours and six sixes. His explosive innings helped India chase down 172 runs and win the first T20I by eight wickets.Iyer’s knock was his first T20I hundred and made him the first Indian captain to score a century while chasing in the format.The previous best belonged to Virat Kohli, who remained unbeaten on 94 from 50 balls against the West Indies in Hyderabad in 2019.Iyer also became only the third Indian captain to score a T20I century. Rohit Sharma had three centuries as captain, while Suryakumar Yadav also reached three figures against South Africa in December 2023.Despite Iyer’s record-breaking effort, he is still some distance behind the overall record for the highest score by a captain in a T20I chase.Pakistan’s Babar Azam remains at the top with 122 from 59 balls against South Africa in Centurion in 2021.Babar’s score was later matched by Singapore captain Aritra Dutta, who also made 122 against Japan in Bangkok in 2024.Iyer’s unbeaten 102 now sits seventh on the all-time list, but his remarkable strike rate of 237.2 makes the innings one of the most explosive captaincy knocks in T20I cricket.

Article Title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has conquered the hype. Now comes the hard part: Waiting
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in action during the Asian Games in Japan. (PTI)

The world sees him differently, and he sees himself differently in the world. What is in his control is the only thing that we can talk about: how he manages himself in this new world that he is in and how he manages the way the world responds to the new Sooryavanshi. Sujith Somasunder | Former India and Karnataka opener

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Sanju Samson (Image credit: Insta)

Someone doesn't become a Player of the Tournament in a World Cup without having the talent. So Sanju Samson has done enough. Gautam Gambhir | Head coach

Lucknow, Oct 06 (ANI): India's Sanju Samson plays a shot during the 1st T20I match against West Indies at Bharat Ratna Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ekana Cricket Stadium, in Lucknow on Tuesday. (ANI Photo)

India's Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in action during the gold medal cricket match between India and Pakistan at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026. (AP Photo/Mark Baker)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: One will have to feel for 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.Whenever VVS Laxman has been at the helm, Sooryavanshi has played for India, be it in Zimbabwe or at the recently concluded 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. To accommodate the teenager in the playing XI, Sanju Samson moved down to No. 3. But with Gautam Gambhir back for the West Indies T20I series, Sooryavanshi has been left warming the bench.The youngster did make his India debut under Gambhir during the tour of England earlier this year, but India's head coach made it clear that Sooryavanshi will have to wait for his opportunity. Gambhir has also made no secret of his faith in Samson, India's Player of the Tournament in the 2026 T20 World Cup. He admitted that leaving the Kerala batter out during India's tour of England was the "toughest decision" he has made since taking charge as head coach.In the first T20I against West Indies, Sooryavanshi was again on the bench, with Samson opening alongside Abhishek Sharma. Samson's stay at the crease lasted only nine balls before he hit a half-tracker straight back to Akeal Hosein. It was a soft dismissal, and in the commentary box, Ian Bishop, one of Samson's many admirers, could not help but question the batter's consistency.The question, then, is where does that leave Sooryavanshi?Sujith Somasunder, former India and Karnataka opener and a sports psychologist, believes the teenager now has to learn how to navigate a world that has changed dramatically since his emergence as one of Indian cricket 's biggest young stars.“Sooryavanshi has achieved what he has achieved so far on his own. Now, suddenly, his status in the cricketing world has moved to a different tangent. The world sees him differently, and he sees himself differently in the world. What is in his control is the only thing that we can talk about: how he manages himself in this new world that he is in and how he manages the way the world responds to the new Sooryavanshi. That is a very important aspect of how he will be able to control and manage this situation,” Somasunder told TimesofIndia.com.“Sooryavanshi has to realise that, ‘I am now going to get into the water, so I need to know how to swim.’ Similarly, he needs to understand that the world I am in now is a little different from what it was before I became Sooryavanshi. He will also need to learn and understand how to navigate this situation for himself,” he added.Sooryavanshi is now fighting for a place in the playing XI with Samson, the man whose 97 not out, 89 and 89 in the knockout stages helped India defend their T20 World Cup title. But since those heroics, Samson has managed only two half-centuries in 11 innings, both coming in Delhi, a venue traditionally favourable to batters. In six of those innings, he has been dismissed for single-digit scores.Sooryavanshi, meanwhile, is still only 15. He has already become a superstar, despite being at the very beginning of his international career. He endured a difficult start against Jofra Archer and Co. in England, but found his groove in Zimbabwe and looked in excellent touch at the Asian Games.Yet Gambhir has drawn a clear line for now. Unless Samson's lean run continues, Sooryavanshi could have to wait longer than expected for another opportunity.Gambhir, however, has stressed that Samson does not need anyone to validate his place in the team, pointing to his performances as proof of his ability.“First of all, he doesn't need to give me any credit (for proper communication when he wasn't playing). His talent itself is enough for him to be in the dressing room. He's shown what he's capable of. Someone doesn't become a Player of the Tournament in a World Cup without having the talent. So he's done enough,” Gambhir said in an interview with Jio Hotstar, praising Samson.“From Vaibhav's point of view, it was again a very clear conversation that he has to wait for his opportunity. We know the kind of talent he has. We know what he can do,” Gambhir had said about Sooryavanshi.For Somasunder, though, the waiting period is not necessarily a setback. It could be an important part of Sooryavanshi's development, provided the teenager is given the right support and guidance.He gives the example of Australia and Ricky Ponting , a prodigiously talented youngster who was identified early as a potential future leader.“In the world of cricket, the way it has gone in India, the onus is always on the individual. In Australia, for example, I remember Ricky Ponting was a very brash young talent. I have heard, though I am not sure if it is true and I have not verified it, that the Australian Institute of Sport, as it was called initially, identified Ricky Ponting as a leader. What they did was take the initiative to groom Ponting as the next captain. He was a very brash young kid, but if they saw that he could be the future captain of the Australian team, then they needed to groom him to behave appropriately and develop the right leadership skills,” he said.Somasunder believes Indian cricket could similarly look beyond simply managing Sooryavanshi's performances and invest in preparing him for the pressures that come with being one of the country's most talked-about young cricketers.“Meanwhile, in our culture, which is relationship-oriented, Australia could be described as more task-oriented. So there are certain nuances to a relationship-oriented culture when it comes to individuals.In a task-oriented culture, there is more individualism. In a hierarchical culture, people tend to bow down to someone higher in the hierarchy. In an individualistic culture, everybody will call themselves by their own name and might even call the coach by his first name,” he added.For Sooryavanshi, this may be his first real lesson in the less glamorous side of international cricket. He has already learnt how to announce himself on the biggest stage. Now, he must learn how to wait for it. At 15, that patience could prove just as important as the talent that got him there in the first place.
Article Summary: 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has been left warming the bench for India. Gautam Gambhir has made no secret of his faith in Samson, India's Player of the Tournament in the 2026 T20 World Cup. Sujith Somasunder, former India and Karnataka opener and a sports psychologist, believes the teenager now has to learn how to navigate a world that has changed.

Article Title: “Do we need Bad Boys t shirts this season?”: Dillon Brooks and John Collins’ massive preseason match fight puts NBA fans in a frenzy
Article Text:
Dillon Brooks and John Collins. Image via: Lon Horwedel / Imagn Images | NBA

Dillon Brooks and John Collins clash early in preseason opener

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NBA fans react to Brooks and Collins scuffle

Dillon Brooks and John Collins needed less than five minutes of Monday night's preseason opener between the Suns and Pistons to put hands on each other. A hard foul on an offensive rebound set it off, and players from both teams stepped in to pull them apart.The penalties were small, but the clip spread quickly, and the reaction split between laughter and disbelief. The Suns forward has a reputation for getting under opponents' skin, and the Pistons forward is the latest to get pulled in. Fans were soon asking whether Detroit needs Bad Boys T-shirts this season.The scrum started with 7:23 left in the first quarter. Collins had pulled down an offensive rebound and looked ready to score when he got hit with a hard foul. After the whistle, the Pistons forward grabbed Brooks by the throat and later pushed the ball into his face.Officials checked the replay and called a flagrant 1 on Collins and a technical on Brooks for unsportsmanlike contact. Lead official Karl Lane said Collins' actions were unnecessary. Phoenix shot two free throws, Detroit shot one, and play went on. ESPN's NBA account posted the clip with a note on the early intensity.It was the first exhibition game of the year for both clubs, played Oct. 5.There were no dirty plays, only small shots that piled up until both men went for the rebound. Many would agree that the throat grab was an overreaction for a preseason game.The clip went viral on the internet, and fans jumped into the comment sections of social media sites for their takes on the matter. Several fans were happy to see the intense drama during the game.@sharonljmoore put the question first: "Do we need Bad Boys t shirts this season?"@TheDreAboveAll went with a welcome: "Oh John Collins.. I was not familiar with this part of your game.. Welcome to Detroit. We'll get you settled in 💯"Timing got plenty of attention, since the game had barely started. @beasthazard92 wrote "Wasn't even 5 mins in 😂" and @PlayoffLucro added "NBA is really back chills 😂". @80sBearfan4life: "Wow this didn't take long and it's only in the preseason 😳"Brooks drew his own share. @Nox384 expects "he's gonna be a menace" this season. Others were less amused. @Rakememes: "This is basketball, not WWE 💀"@ilustriouseller: "grabbing a man neck like that is insane. There is a 6 whole months left in the season. How do you even escalate?"The Pistons secured the 109-107 win over the Suns, but the game will certainly be remembered by the fans and the NBA world.
Article Summary: The Suns forward has a reputation for getting under opponents' skin. Collins had pulled down an offensive rebound and looked ready to score when he got hit with a hard foul. After the whistle, the Pistons forward grabbed Brooks by the throat and later pushed the ball into his face. The Pistons secured the 109-107 win over the Suns.
