Article Title: 'Captaincy ends': Harmanpreet Kaur’s top five achievements as India captain
Article Text:
Harmanpreet Kaur

1. Leading India to its maiden Women’s ODI World Cup title

Harmanpreet Kaur with World Cup title

2. Leading India to back-to-back Asian Games gold medals

Nagoya: India's captain Harmanpreet Kaur, right, and Gunalan Kamalini pose for photographs with Gold medals after winning the women's final T20I cricket match between India and Sri Lanka in the ongoing Asian Games 2026, in Nagoya, Japan. (PTI Photo/Arun Sharma)

3. Winning four Asia Cup titles

Harmanpreet Kaur with Asia Cup trophy

4. Dominating T20I cricket and setting historic leadership milestones

Birmingham: Indian cricket (W) team skipper Harmanpreet Kaur after winning the women's cricket T20 preliminary round match against Pakistan, at the Commonwealth Games (CWG) 2022, in Birmingham, UK. (PTI Photo/R Senthil Kumar)(

5. Leading India to a historic Test victory at Lord’s

Harmanpreet Kaur wants more Test matches after historic win at Lord's (Reuters Photo)

A legacy that goes beyond the numbers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Harmanpreet Kaur ’s decision to step down as captain of the Indian women’s cricket team across all three formats marks the end of one of the longest and most significant leadership eras in Indian women’s cricket.The 37-year-old, who led India’s T20I side for a decade after taking over in 2016, became the ODI captain in 2022 before taking charge across formats in 2023. On Tuesday, she announced that she was ready to move on from leadership and return to playing simply “for the love of the game”.“Captaincy ends. The journey continues,” Harmanpreet wrote in her farewell statement.Her tenure was defined by landmark victories, records and moments that helped shape the modern era of Indian women’s cricket.From finally winning the ODI World Cup to establishing herself among the most successful captains in T20I history, Harmanpreet leaves behind a remarkable leadership legacy.Here are the five biggest achievements of Harmanpreet Kaur’s captaincy stint.The biggest achievement of Harmanpreet Kaur’s captaincy was undoubtedly India’s historic triumph in the Women’s ODI World Cup in November 2025.For decades, an ODI World Cup title had remained one of the biggest missing pieces in Indian women’s cricket.India had come agonisingly close before, finishing runners-up in 2005 and 2017, but the trophy continued to elude the team.That changed under Harmanpreet.Leading India on home soil, she oversaw the campaign that finally delivered the country its first-ever Women’s ODI World Cup title. The achievement carried enormous significance not only for Harmanpreet personally but also for the growth and visibility of women’s cricket in India.The triumph represented the culmination of years of progress. India had developed into a consistent force in international cricket, producing a generation of players capable of competing with the world's best. Harmanpreet's leadership was central to that transition.Winning a World Cup as captain is the defining achievement of any international cricketer. For Harmanpreet, doing so with the Indian women's team made the moment even more significant.The title also ensured that her captaincy legacy would be remembered for more than individual records. She became the leader who helped India cross the final barrier and turn years of promise into a world championship.Another significant achievement of Harmanpreet Kaur’s captaincy was leading India to gold medals at consecutive Asian Games, reinforcing the team’s dominance in the T20 format on the continental stage.India won the women’s cricket gold medal at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou, where cricket made its return to the Games after a long absence. Harmanpreet’s side emerged victorious in the T20 competition, securing India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in women’s cricket.India then successfully defended its title at the 2026 Asian Games, once again finishing at the top of the women’s T20 competition. The back-to-back triumphs highlighted the consistency of the Indian team under Harmanpreet’s leadership and added another pair of major medals to her captaincy résumé.Winning one Asian Games gold was a landmark achievement. Repeating that success four years later demonstrated that India had established itself as the dominant force in the continental competition.Another defining feature of Harmanpreet's captaincy has been India's dominance in the continental game.Under her leadership, India secured four Asia Cup titles, in 2012, 2016, 2022 and 2026, giving Harmanpreet the distinction of being the Indian captain with the most Asia Cup triumphs.The Asia Cup has traditionally been an important tournament for women's cricket in the region, providing teams with an opportunity to test themselves against familiar opponents while also developing younger players.For India, success in the competition has reflected the team's sustained strength.Harmanpreet's four titles also demonstrate the longevity of her leadership. The fact that her successful campaigns stretched across more than a decade is particularly notable. Different teams, different opponents and different generations of Indian players came and went, but Harmanpreet remained a constant presence.The achievement saw her surpass Mithali Raj for the most Asia Cup titles by an Indian captain.That places Harmanpreet in distinguished company. Mithali was one of the central figures of Indian women's cricket for more than two decades, and succeeding her in the record books is a significant marker of Harmanpreet's own influence.The 2026 title was especially important because it came near the end of her captaincy tenure, providing another continental trophy to close one of the most successful leadership chapters in Indian women's cricket.Harmanpreet Kaur’s impact was perhaps most pronounced in T20I cricket, where she spent a decade at the helm after taking over as India’s captain in 2016. Her remarkable longevity not only made her one of the longest-serving leaders in women’s international cricket but also saw her establish several historic records.One of her biggest achievements came when she surpassed Australia’s Meg Lanning to become the captain with the most wins in women’s T20 internationals. The record reflects the consistency and longevity of Harmanpreet’s leadership at a time when the shortest format was undergoing rapid growth around the world.Her T20I tenure also produced another extraordinary milestone. Harmanpreet became the first cricketer in history to captain a side in 150 T20I matches, underlining the remarkable length of her leadership career.Reaching that landmark required far more than simply holding the captaincy. It reflected sustained selection, fitness, performance and, crucially, the confidence of teammates and coaches over many years. During her tenure, women's cricket witnessed the rise of franchise leagues, increasingly demanding international schedules and major tactical developments in T20 cricket.While Harmanpreet's greatest achievements have largely come in limited-overs cricket, one of her most memorable leadership moments arrived in the longest format.She guided India to a dominant 270-run victory over England at Lord's, in the first women's Test match played at the historic London venue.Lord's is one of the most iconic grounds in world cricket, and playing there carries enormous significance regardless of format. For the women's game, the occasion was historic in its own right.India's victory made the event even more memorable.A Test match places very different demands on a captain compared with T20 cricket. Leaders must manage sessions rather than individual overs, balance workloads across multiple days and constantly assess pitch conditions, field placements and bowling changes.Harmanpreet's ability to guide India to a comprehensive victory demonstrated her adaptability as a leader.The 270-run margin also highlighted India's superiority during the match. It was not merely a narrow escape or a hard-fought result; it was a commanding performance at one of cricket's most famous venues.For Harmanpreet, the achievement added another dimension to her captaincy record.Harmanpreet Kaur's decision to step down brings an era to a close, but her contribution to Indian women's cricket will extend far beyond captaincy statistics.She led India through a period of enormous change, from the rapid growth of T20 cricket to the expansion of women's franchise leagues and the eventual breakthrough of a World Cup triumph.Her five standout achievements, the 2025 ODI World Cup, the T20I captaincy wins record, four Asia Cup titles, the 150-match leadership milestone and the historic Lord's Test victory, encapsulate the scale of her tenure.Yet perhaps the most telling part of her farewell was her belief that the team is now “in a good place”.Harmanpreet is stepping away from the leadership role, but not from the game. As she put it, she is now ready to play for the love of cricket again.The captaincy may have ended. The journey, however, continues.
Article Summary: Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down as captain of the Indian women's cricket team. The 37-year-old led India’s T20I side for a decade after taking over in 2016. She became the ODI captain in 2022 before taking charge across formats in 2023.

Article Title: Mumbai's Kalu river throws up hundreds of dead fish, activist blames Ulhasnagar effluent surge
Article Text:
On Sunday morning, hundreds of dead and dying fish were found floating on the Kalu river.





MUMBAI: The sun rose on the Kalu as it did every other day. But on Sunday, along with it rose fish - hundreds, stippling the waters in grisly pointillism. Avinash Harad, an environmental activist who had led a group of six researchers on a biodiversity survey to a site on the river - the ferry crossing at Atali and Nandkar, villages on either side of the Kalu - said hundreds of fish had floated to the surface, dead or dying."The fish died because of untreated effluents from upstream dyeing units in Ulhasnagar that flowed into the Kalu at high tide," Harad said.He said the sluice gates of the KT Dam in Titwala are opened during the rains, bringing a surge of water during high tide that conveys factory discharge downstream. "The fish - mostly catfish and tilapia - died along at least 1 km of the Kalu, just before it meets the Ulhas river."On Sunday morning, Khandu Koli, a fisherman from Nandkar Koliwada in Bhiwandi taluka, was out on the river with 35-40 fishers from Atali and Nandkar, scooping fish out in handheld nets. Koli, whose own family netted 55 kg, said the phenomenon is not uncommon. "But we don't fish when the water turns black," he said.The catch was sold, with a small portion reserved for the fishers' own consumption.Jehu Nadar, a zoologist in the survey group, said prawns had surfaced alongside the fish. Both were dead by 10am.Nadar said the waters were dark green. The team collected samples and found many parameters off the charts: total dissolved solids (TDS) at Atali measured 210 parts per million (ppm), dissolved oxygen (DO) fell to 1.28 mg/L - far below the optimal 6-8 mg/L that aquatic life needs to survive.Upstream at Gurawali Bridge in Titwala , by contrast, TDS was 95.2 ppm and DO 5.53 mg/L."Mystus catfish can tolerate very poor water quality, and tilapia are notoriously tough. If they are turning up dead, the water has reached an absolute zero-survival threshold," Nadar said.The friend of a local fisher who accompanied the group forewarned them of the die-off on Saturday. "He got wind that effluents had been discharged upstream," Nadar said. It was only a matter of time before they surfaced here.
Article Summary: On Sunday morning, hundreds of dead and dying fish were found floating on the Kalu river. The fish died because of untreated effluents from upstream dyeing units in Ulhasnagar. The waters were dark green. The team collected samples and found many parameters off the charts.

Article Title: Oracle donates $10 million to Nashville Symphony; gets thanks note for saving jobs; says: This gift from Oracle is a profound vote of...
Article Text:
Nashville Symphony's season is back, thanks to Oracle.

Oracle's donation saves jobs for 77 musicians and 27 staffers

Nashville Symphony's money troubles came with a sudden leadership change

Oracle's gift buys time while the symphony restructures its finances

Oracle has given $10 million to the Nashville Symphony, a week after the orchestra suspended its 2026/27 season and said it would furlough every one of its musicians. The amount matches the shortfall to the dollar. When the symphony shut the season down, it disclosed a $10 million operating-budget deficit for the fiscal year.The symphony confirmed the gift in a letter to patrons on October 4, saying the season will resume and the furloughs will not go ahead. "This gift from Oracle is a profound vote of confidence in the Nashville Symphony and the important role we play in the cultural fabric of our city," wrote Mark Tillinger, the symphony's president and CEO. The season runs through June 2027.The furloughs were due to begin on October 18 and would have covered all 77 members of the orchestra along with 27 full-time staff. Oracle CEO Clay Magouyrk said the donation allows the symphony to bring all of them back."We are here to help solve the community's problems and ensure Nashville remains a vibrant place to live and work for generations to come," he said. The company is building its new headquarters in the city.According to Tillinger, it was the tech giant that made the first move, asking how it could make "a real, meaningful difference". "We shared what it would take to bring our season and our musicians back, and Oracle met that moment with extraordinary vision and generosity," he said.Ticket holders affected by the cancellations will receive an email with their options. Some concerts are still being reconfirmed, depending on whether guest conductors and artists are available on the original dates.The crisis surfaced on September 28, when the symphony announced the suspension. "The organization has exhausted its cash and cannot continue operating as it has," then CEO J. Mark Cantrell said at the time.Cantrell stepped down days later, about two months into the job. The board replaced him with Tillinger, a former board member. The symphony has not explained why Cantrell left.Tillinger has not presented the money as the end of the problem. He said the symphony will now take on "the difficult but necessary work of restructuring our operations, bringing our costs and revenue into balance." He also told patrons that support from individuals, businesses and community partners remains essential.Nashville is not the only orchestra in this position. Ensembles across the US are still dealing with the after-effects of the pandemic, which sped up the decline of season-ticket subscriptions and left them leaning harder on donors. Last month, Cleveland Orchestra musicians went on a three-day strike over wages, and a strike at the San Francisco Opera cost it its season opener. The Boston Symphony has been in turmoil since it chose not to renew music director Andris Nelsons' contract.The Nashville Symphony plays more than 150 concerts a year, with a focus on contemporary American orchestral music, in a city better known for country. Its two biggest fundraisers, the Symphony Ball on December 12 and the Symphony Fashion Show on April 27, 2027, stayed on the calendar even while the concerts were cancelled. How those nights perform will show whether Oracle's $10 million marks the start of a recovery or only rescues this season.
Article Summary: Oracle gives $10 million to the Nashville Symphony. Symphony suspended its 2026/27 season and said it would furlough every one of its musicians. Oracle CEO Clay Magouyrk said the donation allows the symphony to bring all of them back.

Article Title: Xbox secures exclusive GTA 6 streaming rights ahead of launch: All details
Article Text:
Image via Rockstar Games

A cloud route to PC

A counter to PlayStation's marketing push

Timing: Streaming limits arrive in November

Microsoft’s Xbox has reportedly landed exclusive cloud streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), a move that could give PC gamers access to the highly anticipated title at launch even though Rockstar Games has yet to announce a PC version. According to a report by The Verge, Xbox Cloud Gaming will be the only cloud service allowed to stream GTA 6 when the game launches. The duration of the reported exclusivity agreement remains unclear. The report said Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told employees during an all-hands meeting that Microsoft was preparing to do something around GTA 6 that “no other platform holder is doing.” Sources familiar with the company’s plans told The Verge that the comment referred to Xbox securing exclusive streaming rights for the game.The biggest effect may be on PC players. Rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA 6, and The Verge said the deal lets Xbox pitch its cloud service to PC players who would otherwise need an Xbox Series X/S or a PS5. That means the game could be playable on PC in November through cloud streaming, though it would not be a native PC release.For anyone weighing a console purchase just for GTA 6, the deal could provide another way in.For Microsoft, it is a chance to promote Xbox Cloud Gaming on a title that is expected to dominate the holiday season.GTA 6 is set to launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. PlayStation holds the marketing deal for the game. Many ads say it "plays best on PS5." The reported streaming exclusivity gives Xbox its own GTA 6 selling point after that PlayStation-led campaign.The report lands as Xbox Cloud Gaming is about to change. The Verge reports that starting in November, monthly cloud gaming access will be capped at 15 hours for Game Pass Ultimate subscribers, 10 hours for Premium subscribers and five hours for Essential subscribers. Those limits could matter for a game as large as GTA 6, where long sessions are common.To offset the caps, players will be able to buy bundles of streaming hours without needing a Game Pass subscription. Microsoft has not announced prices. One unconfirmed rumour puts the cost at $5.99 for 25 streaming hours.
Article Summary: Microsoft's Xbox has reportedly landed exclusive cloud streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) The move could give PC gamers access to the highly anticipated title at launch even though Rockstar Games has yet to announce a PC version. The duration of the reported exclusivity agreement remains unclear.

Article Title: In 1992, Larry Ellison shattered his elbow in a bicycle crash; after a UC Davis surgeon repaired it, the Oracle co-founder gave $5 million to help others with bone and muscle disorders
Article Text:
Oracle founder Larry Ellison

Record-setting donation made by Larry Ellison

What the money built

A serious bicycle accident suffered by Oracle CEO Larry Ellison in the early 1990s ultimately resulted in a $5 million donation that helped expand research into bone and muscle disorders at UC Davis, according to the university. The Oracle co-founder's gift helped build a musculoskeletal research and care program at UC Davis that is still part of the university's orthopaedic identity. Ellison, the co-founder and longtime chief executive of Oracle, shattered his elbow in a bicycle crash in 1992. The injury was treated by Michael Chapman, an orthopaedic surgeon at UC Davis, who successfully reconstructed the damaged joint. Following the surgery, Ellison donated $5 million to support musculoskeletal research and patient care at the university.The gift helped establish what became the Lawrence J. Ellison Musculoskeletal Research Center, where physicians, surgeons and scientists work on research aimed at preventing and treating musculoskeletal disorders. According to UC Davis, the centre focuses on conditions affecting bones, muscles and joints, bringing together experts from multiple disciplines.UC Davis announced the pledge in September 1995, when it reported record private giving of $41.5 million for fiscal year 1994-95.That was a 39 percent increase over the $29.8 million raised the year before. Ellison, then CEO of Oracle, made the largest single gift of the year. The $5 million pledge was meant to create three endowed chairs and a musculoskeletal institute in the School of Medicine."Mr. Ellison's generosity in particular will help sustain our nationally recognized expertise and care for patients with bone or muscle diseases," said Gerald S. Lazarus, then dean of the School of Medicine. The School of Medicine received $12.7 million in private support that year, an 88 percent increase. The university said this was the largest amount ever given to an academic unit on the campus.The Ellison center brings together physicians, surgeons and basic scientists. They study the prevention and treatment of what UC Davis calls "crippling and painful musculoskeletal disorders."A 2011 UC Davis Health profile described the center as part of a broader orthopaedic and sports medicine program. Its specialists have served as team doctors for the NBA's Sacramento Kings for more than two decades. The same program provides care for Olympic-level athletes, the national soccer program and UC Davis teams. US News & World Report ranked UC Davis among the nation's best hospitals for orthopaedics.Paul Di Cesare, then chair of orthopaedic surgery, said the program uses the same advanced techniques for professionals and ordinary patients. "We use those same modalities and treatments for the average athlete and the weekend warrior," he said.
Article Summary: Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison shattered his elbow in a bicycle crash in 1992. Ellison donated $5 million to support musculoskeletal research and patient care at UC Davis. The gift helped establish what became the Lawrence J. Ellison Musculo-Oriental Research Center.

Article Title: A Welsh man climbed Snowdon 141 times in one year dressed as Spider-Man; he raised £6,188 for children with life-threatening illnesses
Article Text:
Image: Cambrian news

How Dylan Hughes began the Spider-Man challenge

Snow, heat and difficult mountain conditions

His 100th climb became a family milestone

He crossed Crib Goch 108 times

£6,118 went to Hope House

Spider-Man helped him connect with walkers

The challenge could return in 2027

A Welsh father turned one of Britain's most recognisable mountains into the backdrop for an extraordinary year-long fundraising challenge, climbing Snowdon 141 times while dressed as Spider-Man. Dylan Hughes, from Bangor, Gwynedd, took on the challenge throughout 2025 to raise money for Hope House Tŷ Gobaith children's hospices, which support children with life-threatening conditions and their families. His unusual costume quickly became part of the challenge, attracting attention from fellow walkers and helping him spread awareness of the charity during his repeated journeys to the summit. Hughes eventually raised £6,118, according to Hope House, and presented the charity with a cheque in January 2026. The challenge also included 108 crossings of the difficult Crib Goch ridge, adding another demanding element to his year of fundraising.Dylan Hughes, a father of two from Bangor, Gwynedd, had already developed a strong connection with the mountains of Eryri before beginning his fundraising challenge. In 2025, he decided to combine that interest with a year-long effort for Hope House Tŷ Gobaith, choosing Yr Wyddfa, commonly known as Snowdon, as the centre of his campaign.Hughes climbed to the summit 141 times during the year while wearing a Spider-Man costume, turning himself into a highly recognisable figure on the mountain. Hope House said the costume helped him attract the attention of fellow walkers, who would stop to take photographs and talk to him about the reason behind the challenge. Hughes used those encounters to explain the work of the children's hospice and encourage donations. The challenge continued through different seasons and weather conditions, eventually producing 141 summit ascents and a substantial fundraising total.Completing 141 ascents of Yr Wyddfa required Hughes to repeatedly face changing conditions throughout the year, from deep winter snow to warmer summer weather. Hope House reported that some of his winter climbs involved snow reaching up to his waist, forcing him to make his own path through sections of the mountain. During the summer, the conditions were more favourable but the mountain became busier, giving Hughes more opportunities to interact with other walkers while wearing the Spider-Man costume. His repeated journeys also meant returning to the mountain regardless of the conditions and maintaining the challenge over an entire calendar year. The unusual sight of Spider-Man climbing towards the summit became familiar to people visiting Eryri, with Hughes able to turn many of those encounters into conversations about the children and families supported by Hope House.One of the most significant moments came on July 19, 2025, when Hughes completed his 100th ascent of Yr Wyddfa alongside his seven-year-old son, Jac. It was Jac's first time reaching the summit, making the milestone particularly meaningful for Hughes after months of climbing the mountain as part of his fundraising effort. By that point, he had raised around £3,600 for Hope House and had also completed 69 crossings of Crib Goch. Hope House later identified the climb with his son as Hughes' fondest memory of the entire challenge. The occasion gave the year-long project a family dimension, as Hughes was able to share one of his mountain journeys with his son rather than marking the 100th summit solely as a personal endurance achievement.Alongside his 141 ascents of Yr Wyddfa, Hughes completed 108 crossings of Crib Goch, the narrow and exposed ridge on the Snowdon massif. The ridge is known for its steep, rocky terrain and exposure, making it a particularly demanding part of the mountain for walkers. Hughes submitted details of his 108 crossings to Guinness World Records because he believed the achievement could qualify for a new record. When Hope House published its account of his fundraising achievement in January 2026, Guinness had not yet officially confirmed the record, meaning the 108 crossings should be regarded as an achievement submitted for consideration rather than a ratified Guinness World Record. The crossings nevertheless formed a major part of Hughes' challenge and added another physical test to a year in which he repeatedly travelled to the summit of Snowdon.Hughes ultimately raised £6,118 for Hope House Tŷ Gobaith, presenting a cheque to the charity at Tŷ Gobaith on January 16, 2026. Hope House Children's Hospices supports children with life-threatening conditions and their families across North Wales, Shropshire, Cheshire and surrounding areas, with Tŷ Gobaith serving families in North Wales. The money raised by Hughes will help the charity provide services including respite stays, which give families time away from the pressures of caring for a seriously ill child, as well as physiotherapy and activity sessions that can provide children with positive experiences and opportunities to make memories with their families. Hughes also visited Tŷ Gobaith and met children and families supported by the hospice, giving him an opportunity to see directly how the money from his mountain challenge could help.The Spider-Man costume became an important part of Hughes' fundraising strategy because it made his challenge immediately recognisable to people on the mountain. Hope House said he met walkers from different parts of the world during his climbs, with conversations often beginning because people wanted to know why a person dressed as the comic-book superhero was repeatedly climbing Snowdon. Those encounters produced a number of memorable moments during the year. Hughes recalled seeing someone climbing the mountain wearing only Speedos, while he also narrowly missed encountering former heavyweight boxing champion Tyson Fury and his family during one of his outings. His Facebook presence documenting his Eryri adventures also helped draw attention to the campaign, allowing the unusual sight of Spider-Man on the mountain to become associated with fundraising for Hope House.Completing the 141st climb in 2025 did not necessarily mark the end of Hughes' fundraising relationship with Snowdon or Hope House. In its January 2026 account, the charity reported that he planned to return in 2027 and repeat the challenge for the children's hospices. His 2025 effort had already transformed repeated journeys up Yr Wyddfa into a fundraising campaign that combined endurance, family memories and public awareness. From battling through waist-deep snow to completing his 100th summit with his son and crossing Crib Goch 108 times, Hughes used the mountain as a platform to raise £6,118 for children with life-threatening conditions. The Spider-Man costume made him a familiar sight to walkers, while the money ultimately went towards services intended to support children and give their families vital respite and positive experiences.
Article Summary: Dylan Hughes, from Bangor, Gwynedd, took on the challenge throughout 2025 to raise money for Hope House Tŷ Gobaith children's hospices. His unusual costume quickly became part of the challenge, attracting attention from fellow walkers and helping him spread awareness of the charity. Hughes eventually raised £6,118, according to Hope House, and presented the charity with a cheque in January 2026.

Article Title: For every 30 Chinese AI researchers moving to the US, only one went to China; migration expert warns: The danger for the US is...
Article Text:
30 Chinese AI researchers move to US for every 1 going to China: Carnegie study

China now produces more top AI researchers than any other country

A booming home industry and travel curbs are keeping Chinese AI talent at home

South Korea and Singapore are the other big winners in the AI talent race

The US-China race for artificial intelligence is usually measured in chips and frontier models. A new study measures it in people, and the flow still runs heavily one way. For every 30 Chinese-origin AI researchers working in the United States in 2025, only one US-trained researcher was working in China, according to the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. In 2022, that ratio stood at 46 to one.The gap is narrowing, but slowly, and a migration expert says the headline number may be hiding the real problem. "The danger for the U.S. is a slow erosion of its appeal to attract talent that compounds over decades," said Yingyi Ma, a sociology professor at Syracuse University who studies Asian students in America. "By the time the effect shows up in the data, it is hard to reverse."Her point rests on timing. The study tracks where researchers studied and where they work now, but not when they moved. Most made that call years before the Trump administration tightened student visas, added a $100,000 fee to new H-1B petitions and cut federal research funding.For now, the US still wins the head count. The share of Chinese-origin talent among AI researchers working in America rose four percentage points to about 36%, said Damien Ma, director of Carnegie China, who led the study.The US recorded a net gain of 2,145 elite researchers, while China posted a net loss of 1,729.The study, titled "Who's Ahead in the Global AI Talent Race?", follows 10,280 authors whose papers were accepted at NeurIPS 2025, one of the most selective machine learning conferences in the world. The team traced each author's undergraduate degree, graduate school and current employer, using Claude Code and OpenAI Codex to process the data with human checks at every stage.The results show how fast China's base has grown. Scientists who earned undergraduate degrees in China made up 57% of the sample, up 11 percentage points since 2022, while the US share fell to 13%. China has also overtaken the US as the top place where this talent works, at 41% against 34%.Universities tell the same story. Peking University ranked first for AI research output, followed by Tsinghua. Google, which topped the 2022 list, slipped to seventh. Twelve Chinese institutions made the top 30, double the count three years earlier.Retention is where China has gained the most. Around 69% of China-trained researchers now work in China, up from 57% in 2022, though that still trails the US at 89%.Part of the pull is prestige. Kevin Xu, founder of hedge fund Interconnected Capital, said a job at DeepSeek now carries the same professional weight as one at OpenAI, a big shift from five years ago.Part of it is control. Beijing barred the two founders of Manus from leaving the country after Meta agreed to buy the startup, and later ordered the deal unwound. Last month, reports said travel curbs on top AI and chip executives at private firms had been widened to require government approval even for short trips by their spouses and children.China has also tried to court outsiders, launching a K visa for young STEM graduates in October 2025. It has not worked so far. Only 118 researchers trained elsewhere moved to work in China, per the study. Returnees remain rare, though Tencent's hiring of former OpenAI researcher Yao Shunyu as chief AI scientist stood out.Away from the two superpowers, smaller Asian hubs are pulling ahead. South Korea keeps 77% of its homegrown AI researchers, the second-highest retention rate after the US. KAIST jumped 12 places to rank third among the top 30 institutions.Singapore has become a magnet of its own. It posted a net gain of 218 researchers, second only to America, and many of those arrivals came from China. National University of Singapore and Nanyang Technological University both broke into the top 20, while Europe's ETH Zurich and Oxford dropped off the list altogether.Which brings the story back to the 30-to-one figure. It reflects choices made before the visa crackdown, and on that count America remains the clear winner. Whether the next cohort chooses the same way is what the data cannot show yet.
Article Summary: China now produces more top AI researchers than any other country. For every 30 Chinese-origin AI researchers working in the U.S. in 2025, only one US-trained researcher was working in China. South Korea and Singapore are the other big winners in the AI talent race.

Article Title: At Purana Qila, shastriya nritya took centre stage
Article Text:
Kalakshetra Foundation presented Gangadhara, a Bharatanatyam production exploring different aspects of Shiva.

Grace meets the grandeur of Purana Qila

Celebrating classical arts legacy

Raja Reddy and Kapil Mishra; Suneel Anchipaka

Natya Tarangini students presented a Kuchipudi recital

Of poses and poise: An Odissi recital by the Sutra Foundation from Kuala Lumpur

Madhavi Mudgal

Ramli Ibrahim

Choreographed by Kathak exponent Vaswati Misra, students from Dhwani presented The Hero in Shades





The sounds of ghungroos echoed in the Purana Qila precinct as the second edition of the Indraprastha Nritya Mahotsav unfolded over the weekend.Organised by Delhi Tourism, the three-day festival aims to celebrate India’s classical dance traditions while placing them against the historical setting of one of Delhi’s oldest landmarks.A light-and-sound presentation tracing the story of Indraprastha and the Yamuna formed part of the evening, with a voiceover bringing the qila into the narrative: “Main ek viraat imaarat hun, meri oonche dwaar aur vishaal diwaare aaj bhi bhavyata aur shakti ki kahaani sunaate hain... Mere bheetar ab bhi goonjte hain anginat geet, jo samay ki thapedon ke beech, jeevan ki atoot dhara ko bahaye rakhte hain..."This year, the festival bought together more than 150 dancers from India and abroad. Speaking about it, Suneel Anchipaka, MD & CEO, Delhi Tourism and Transportation Development Corporation (DTTDC), said, “Set against the magnificent backdrop of Purana Qila, this festival beautifully brings together Delhi’s heritage and India’s vibrant classical dance traditions. We hope to create a greater awareness and appreciation of these art forms among Delhi’s residents and international tourists.Kapil Mishra, Delhi’s Tourism and Culture Minister, spoke about the city’s long and layered history. “This is a city whose history goes back to when human civilisation began. Delhi has remained a centre of power and through such initiatives it will continue to remain a centre for culture," he said.On day 1, students of Natya Tarangini, under the guidance of Kuchipudi exponents Raja Radha Reddy and Kaushalya Reddy presented two pieces, including Maha Prana Deepam Shivam featuring different rhythmic patterns and Shivoham, drew from the six verses composed by Adi Shankaracharya that explain the essence of Advaita Vedanta.Directed by Ramli Ibrahim, the Sutra Foundation from Kuala Lumpur, presented Fragrant Odissi, showcasing works inspired by the Guru Debaprasad Odissi tradition. The presentation opened with a traditional Mangalacharan, a tribute to Durga, and it was followed by Odia abhinaya, Muha Mukhi KishoraKalakshetra Foundation presented Gangadhara, a Bharatanatyam production exploring different aspects of Shiva. The presentation featured Thunga Tharange Gange, followed by a Padam, depicting Nataraja’s blissful dance at Chidambaram. The performance concluded with a Thillana showcasing intricate footworkChoreographed by Kathak exponent Vaswati Misra, students from Dhwani presented The Hero in Shades. It was a Kathak production that explored the complex character of Lord Krishna through episodes from the Mahabharata. The story was narrated through the voice of a woman who serves as a priestess at a Krishna temple. Looking at rituals, faith and the epic from a 20th-century perspective, the production questioned the roles of its heroes and heroines, inviting the audience to reflect on Krishna’s many shadesDays two and three featured Bharatanatyam by Parshwanath Upadhye and Aditya P V, Sattriya by Guru Anita Sharma and her group, Mohiniyattam and Kathakali by Guru Pallavi Krishnan, Kathak by Guru Shama Bhate and her group, Folk Chhand by artistes from Delhi, Odissi by Nrityagram, Bengaluru, led by Guru Surupa Sen, Manipuri by Guru Latasana Devi and her group, and a specially composed Bharatanatyam finale by Guru Vaibhav Arekar.
Article Summary: The Indraprastha Nritya Mahotsav took place in the Purana Qila precinct of Delhi. Organised by Delhi Tourism, the three-day festival aims to celebrate India’s classical dance traditions. More than 150 dancers from India and abroad took part in the festival.

Article Title: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke shares 'mid-flight diaries' ahead of Delhi protest: 'Tired of seeing fear in my mother's eyes'
Article Text:
Cockroach Janata Party founder Abhijeet Dipke being welcomed by his mother (File Photo/ANI)

Dipke's Instagram Post

Dipke alleges police pressure ahead of protest

'Why is Fadnavis trying to be Yogi Adityanath 2.0?'

Three demands over EC, SIR





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said his mother cried as he left home for Delhi ahead of the October 10 protest, seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Dipke shared a post on Wednesday captioned "Mid-flight diaries," in which he spoke about his parents’ concerns and the fear faced by those taking part in protests."As I left home today, Mom cried as if I was heading to a war zone. She knows I’m going to Delhi from Bengaluru and that I won’t be home before the October 10 protest," Dipke wrote."I could see the fear in her eyes. And like always, I lied. I told her she was being paranoid, that she was worrying for no reason, that everything would be fine."Dipke said he was "tired of seeing that fear" in his mother’s eyes and of reassuring her when he himself did not know what the coming days would bring."But I’m tired of seeing that fear in my mother’s eyes. Tired of giving her assurances when even I don’t know what the next few days will bring," he said.He also described his father’s silence as he leaves for the protest."Tired of watching my dad stand there in complete silence, saying nothing, but somewhere wishing we could just go back to the life we had three months ago," Dipke said.He said the anxiety was not limited to his own family."And I know it’s not just my parents," he wrote. "Every one of you who has chosen to speak up, step out of your homes and take to the streets probably knows this feeling.""The worried calls. The constant messages asking where you are. The fear they try not to show because they know how much this means to you."Dipke said those participating in the protests should know that they were not alone."I just want you to know that you are not alone. None of us are. We are all in this together," he said.He said he hoped for an India where parents would not have to fear for their children when they chose to protest."And I hope we can build an India where, someday, when our own children take to the streets to raise their voices, we won’t have to fear for their lives the way our parents fear for ours today," Dipke said.Addressing parents, he said: "And to all the parents, please don’t stop us today. We understand your fear. We know where it comes from. We know what we are putting you through.""But we are tired of living in constant fear," he said.Dipke on Tuesday accused the BJP-led central government of using 'One Nation, One Election' as a step towards what he described as "one nation, one political party".Ahead of the October 10 agitation at Jantar Mantar, Dipke alleged that police in Maharashtra’s Chandrapur district had issued notices to CJP activists and pressured them not to attend the planned protest."One Nation, One Election is just a slogan. The actual intention of the ruling dispensation is to push the country toward 'one nation, one political party'," Dipke said.He alleged that the "true objective" behind one nation, one election was to "snatch away the voting rights guaranteed to citizens by Dr B R Ambedkar"."This is not about one party or ideology, it is a fight for the survival of Indian democracy," he said.Dipke said he had seen two notices issued by police in Chandrapur and alleged that similar notices had been issued in Rajasthan by the local CID to a person named Mukesh, warning him of legal action if he attended the October 10 protest."I have said multiple times that the Maharashtra Police is the best police force in the country, and the Delhi Police should learn from them. But it is heart-breaking that the Chandrapur police served notices to CJP workers, asking them not to participate in the protest at Jantar Mantar," he said."They also asked CJP workers about the source of funds for travelling to Jantar Mantar," Dipke said."The police stated (in the notice) that the agitation is going to be "violent". How do the police know so early that the agitation would be violent? Have they planned anything in advance?" he asked."Why is the Maharashtra Police behaving like Delhi Police? What do they have to do if a person is going to Delhi from Chandrapur?" he said.Targeting Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Dipke said he should be aware of the state’s legacy."Why Devendra Fadnavis is trying to be UP CM Yogi Adityanath 2.0? He should know about the legacy of Maharashtra. He should not disrespect and misuse the Maharashtra Police for political ambitions," he said."Instead of harassing our workers, they should arrest me...If they want they should put me behind the bars and charge me with UAPA, NSA. They should not harass our workers," Dipke said.He also criticised police directions to CJP activists against posting anything on social media that could lead to violence."We speak about (Mahatma) Gandhi and B R Ambedkar. Do they think it is violent?" he asked.Dipke alleged that Rahul Pawara, who is leading a protest by tribal students in Maharashtra, was also facing police harassment."Yesterday, the Adivasi students led by Rahul Pawara faced repression in Mumbai and some students were beaten up. If the son of Ambani or an MP, MLA was protesting, would the police behave in such a manner?" he asked.He said Pawara was fighting for better education for tribal students.Dipke also said Maharashtra Police had once been compared with Scotland Yard because of its efficiency and urged the force to maintain that image.On the MPSC agitation, Dipke said aspirants were demanding leak-proof examinations, accountability and action against those responsible for paper leaks.He also questioned the appointment of Vivek Bhimanwar as MPSC chairman by the Governor."Why did the Governor appoint the Chief Minister's friend as Chairman of MPSC?....I am very sorry to say this, but in this era, the Governor is merely a puppet of those who are sitting in the government," Dipke said.He reiterated that the entire country would become Jantar Mantar if Gyanesh Kumar was not removed as CEC."We have three demands. First is the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar, along with that, he should be booked under criminal charges and the SIR should be stopped," Dipke said."The last demand is that the appointment of Election Commissioner should be done independently and neutrally," he said.He added that the Election Commission should not be merely the "choice of Amit Shah and Narendra Modi."
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said his mother cried as he left home for Delhi ahead of the October 10 protest. Dipke shared a post on Wednesday captioned "Mid- flight diaries," in which he spoke about his parents’ concerns and the fear faced by those taking part in protests. He also described his father’s silence as he leaves for the protest.

Article Title: And thereby hangs a tale! Jeffrey Archer’s Delhi connect
Article Text:
(File photo) Jeffrey Archer at a Delhi event a few years ago

TOI





NEW DELHI: A Delhi traffic signal was the starting point of a love story in Jeffrey Archer’s ‘Caste-Off’. Jamwal and Nisha fall for each other while waiting for the light to turn green.Archer, the English novelist and politician who died Monday at 86, had connections with the Indian capital beyond the pages of his books. He met readers at a Delhi airport book-signing session in 2015 and addressed an audience ranging from children to senior citizens at Siri Fort Auditorium in 2019.The city also made an impression on him beyond its fictional possibilities.Asked what he liked about Delhi in a June 2010 interview with, Archer praised the layout of its centre and its parliamentary precinct. “I was very impressed with that,” he said.His admiration was coupled with amusement at Delhi’s traffic scene. In the same interview, he expressed astonishment at the nature of Indian driving and joked about motorists’ treatment of lane markings.At the interactive session at Siri Fort, he discussed ‘Kane and Abel’, his debut novel ‘Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less’, and the origins of ‘The Clifton Chronicles’, before signing books for his Delhi fans.For some in that audience, the memories have proved as enduring as Archer’s books. Sonalika Paul, an avid reader and private-sector employee who has since moved to Canada, still remembers an anecdote he shared that evening.He recalled a boy approaching his car in Mumbai with a stack of books and asking whether he wanted the latest Jeffrey Archer. The author’s response: “I am the latest Jeffrey Archer.”Paul says, “That story stayed with me. In that one exchange, you could see both his humour and how far his books had travelled.”The evening at Siri Fort also offered readers a glimpse of the man behind his plot twists. Archer opened with cricket, speaking about Indian players and praising Virat Kohli, before describing a writing routine that still involved putting every word down by hand. For aspiring authors, there was also a reminder of the persistence behind his success: he recalled 16 publishers rejecting his first novel and spoke of the years of work, determination and luck that a writing career demanded.For Dr Jonathan Koshy Varghese, assistant professor of English at DU’s Lady Shri Ram College, Archer was among the authors who introduced him to a wider world of books as a teenager. His novels were discoveries made in school libraries, bridging changing reading tastes. “I read him when I was bored with Enid Blyton and when I needed something lighter than Mario Puzo,” he says.For Varghese, Archer’s death closes a chapter in a generation’s reading life, even as its readers continue to turn to other books. “Archer represented a kind of reading that was guilt-free,” the professor says — an inexpensive indulgence, enjoyed for the sheer pleasure of reading a good story.That connection with readers helped turn Archer’s releases into eagerly awaited events. Aninda Das, who has worked with leading publishing houses, recalls the anticipation whenever a new Archer title reached bookstores. “An Archer book hitting bookshelves was an occasion in itself, and that excitement has endured for decades,” he said, describing the lasting affection and loyalty that the author commanded among Indian readers.For avid reader Piyush Amola, Archer’s appeal began with the urge to turn another page. “With Archer, you always wanted to know what happened next. His language was easy, but his plots kept you guessing,” he says. The ambition, rivalries and family loyalties made the stories feel familiar, Amola adds, even when they unfolded in worlds far removed from his own. “You finished one book and looked forward to the next.”
Article Summary: Archer, the English novelist and politician who died Monday at 86, had connections with the Indian capital beyond the pages of his books. He met readers at a Delhi airport book-signing session in 2015 and addressed an audience ranging from children to senior citizens in 2019.

Article Title: Insect fans want 'bugging' to become the new birding
Article Text:
Meehir Pawar's nature trails spotlight insects , 11-year-old Viyaan Bhatia feeds his ants an orange





People huddled in groups, necks craned upward, are a common sight in parks and forests these days. Now, a new group pose can be spotted in the urban outdoors: people crouching low, their gaze locked on the ground. They're not birding but 'bugging'.Insects have crawled into the city's nature calendar, with walks, talks and camps organised around beetles, moths, dragonflies, and stinkbugs—calling attention to a class of organisms that, despite its outsize numbers and diversity, has long been overlooked for its undersized dimensions. Entomologists and nature educators are trying to correct this anomaly."More people are now turning to insects because they are a close and accessible subject and offer a variety that no other subject can," says V. Shubhalaxmi, an entomologist who has been conducting workshops and walks for two decades.That variety is much greater than previously thought: a major study published this June estimates that there could be 14-20 million insect species in the world, more than double previous estimates. (By comparison, birds log 11,131 species.) Only 1.2 million species have been formally described so far.Advanced phone cameras have helped bring bugs into focus. Several budget smartphones today have macro lenses that allow people to magnify insects as small as weevils and closely observe the dazzling diversity of their shapes, colours and patterns, says Meehir Pawar, a recipient of Sanctuary's Young Naturalist Award and expert in dragonflies and damselflies.The ability to observe the 5mm triangular head of an Indian Grass Mantis or the translucent margins of the Indian Green Tortoise Beetle fosters a new appreciation for these overlooked creatures. "A common reaction people have to bugs is fear and repulsion," Meehir notes. But when they learn more about them, including their benefits as decomposers, pollinators and pest controllers, the reaction "changes to awe and appreciation".Learning about bugs also dispels myths, such as the belief that dragonflies sting with their tails (they don't).Children are drawn deeper than adults. It's probably because this generation hasn't been exposed to 'insectophobia', says Shubhalaxmi, adding that children also have more opportunities to experience nature first-hand, along with access to online knowledge.Viyaan Bhatia, an 11-year-old from Chembur, is closely acquainted with ants. He has raised several colonies at home, inspired by a YouTube video. "It took me a while to identify a queen ant in my compound," he says. The first queen he collected, of the Indian black ant species, produced an all-male brood. The second, incubated in a test-tube, produced females, but the colony perished in an attack by ghost ants. Viyaan is now raising six colonies at a time. His friends haven't been bitten by the bug but are willing to halt a game when he spots a queen.Entomologist Eshaan Pahade is doing his bit to spread the bug. In 2023, he set up the Entomon Institute of Invertebrate Zoology to focus on research and communication, and this Jan launched a series of online courses on everything from insect behaviour to forensic entomology, which studies arthropods as evidence in death investigations. He's had participants from age 7 to 82 sign up.Today, several forums exist for people to discuss insects, such as InsectIndia, a Facebook group to which Pahade belongs, which has 46,000 members. "Around 2,000 are active," he estimates. Even within the insectiverse, specialisations exist, with subgroups dedicated to ants, butterflies, moths—and beetles.Nonprofit India's Nature runs an annual campaign called Beetle Mania to celebrate and document Coleoptera, the largest order of all animals, with nearly 400,000 species described. India has an estimated 22,299 species, according to the Zoological Survey of India."There is a real, measurable gap in citizen science coverage of beetles in India," says co-founder Ramnarayan Kalyanaraman. "Butterflies average about 461 research grade observations per species on iNaturalist; beetles average about 24." This gap is due to a dearth of popular literature and field guides, especially in vernacular languages, and of outreach groups, he adds. Beetles also have a negative association from their role as crop and property pests (like the cotton boll weevil).Beetle Mania aims to change this. The campaign, the 5th edition of which ran this year from Aug 22 to Sep 13, conducted webinars and encouraged participants to document what they saw. They're currently inviting species nominations for a Beetles of India pamphlet they're assembling, complete with regional names and local folklore.Folklore helps connect people both to nature and to oral storytelling, says Jennifer Divyadarshi, co-founder of India's Nature. "Natural historians are also storytellers—they observe a landscape and its beings but also help people understand what they are seeing. Stories are a good way to do that. For people working with rural communities, hearing their perspectives and ways of seeing nature reveals deep relationships," she says.There's another, more pressing reason to look closely at insects: they are early indicators of threatened ecosystems and climate change. Shubhalaxmi compares them to the first-floor occupants of a 3-storey building developing cracks from the ground up: "We need to spot and fix the cracks early on before they reach the terrace, where humans reside, and the building collapses. More research on the impacts of climate change on insects could provide this fix. "
Article Summary: Insects have crawled into the city's nature calendar, with walks, talks and camps organised around beetles, moths, dragonflies, and stinkbugs. Entomologists and nature educators are trying to correct this anomaly. India has an estimated 22,299 species, according to the Zoological Survey of India.

Article Title: ​Two fined for water wastage in Sambhajinagar; Action begins before Oct 15 deadline
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





As drought threatens to deepen the city’s water crisis, the civic body has begun cracking down on wastage ahead of its Oct 15 deadline to repair leaking taps and pipelines. Two residents were fined, and 33 illegal water connections snapped on Tuesday.The Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation (CSMC) has asked citizens to fix leaking taps, domestic connections and internal pipelines by Oct 15. However, municipal commissioner Amol Yedge has ordered field action already as the civic body looks to conserve every drop in a drought year.During patrols in Aref Colony and Hilal Colony, water supply department teams spotted two residents wasting tap water. One was fined Rs 10,000 for allowing water to flow onto the road. Another was fined Rs 5,000 for failing to repair a tap and allowing water to go waste.“We once again appeal to citizens to close taps after filling and ensure water does not flow into drains or roads. It is our collective responsibility to save water during the current drought situation, failing which the water crisis could aggravate further,” Yedge said.After Oct 15, the corporation will impose a graded penalty for water wastage. A first violation will attract a Rs 5,000 fine and a second Rs 10,000. A third violation will invite a Rs 25,000 penalty along with a criminal case.The civic body has also turned its attention to water theft.On Tuesday, a special squad disconnected 33 illegal water connections in Nagsen Colony, Roshan Gate and Asifiya Colony. The team found unauthorised connections tapped into a 200mm main pipeline. These were also causing heavy leakage, apart from water theft.CSMC has warned that illegal connections will not be tolerated. It plans to intensify the drive across the city.
Article Summary: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation (CSMC) has asked citizens to fix leaking taps, domestic connections and internal pipelines by Oct 15. Two residents were fined, and 33 illegal water connections snapped on Tuesday. A first violation will attract a Rs 5,000 fine and a second Rs 10,000.

Article Title: Ghaygaon oil unit fails FDA test, seizes stock worth Rs23L
Article Text:
Alleged substandard and misbranded stock of 10,798.4 kg of refined palmolein oil worth Rs 23,32,455 seized by the FDA.

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:

Action against dairy in same taluka





Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended licence of an oil repacking unit at Vaijapur under ‘Safe Food Safe Maharashtra’ campaign .Suspecting the stock to be substandard and misbranded, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) seized 10,798.4kg of refined palmolein oil worth Rs 23,32,455 from a unit on Gangapur Road at Ghaygaon.The action was taken by a team led by food safety officer Pragya Surse during an inspection of the unit, which was found violating FSSAI norms and maintaining poor hygiene standards. The unit scored only 36 out of 86 marks (42%) and was declared Non-Compliant, FDA officials said.“The floor was found oily and broken, packing material and food articles were stored openly on the ground, and iron tanks were used instead of mandatory stainless steel tanks. Drinking water used for production had no test report as per IS:10500 standard,” FDA joint commissioner Shrikaant Karkale said.He added, “Doors were kept open and windows had no insect-proof nets, posing a risk of contamination. No proper pest control system was in place, workers had no hand gloves and aprons, and no trained staff was present. Temperature control records were also not maintained.”In another action in Vaijapur, the FDA suspended the licence of a dairy unit in Yashwant Colony over unhygienic conditions.The unit scored only 15 out of 94 marks (16%). FDA officials found broken floors, open doors, plastic cans being used instead of stainless steel tanks, no system for checking milk and no Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP).The FDA seized and destroyed 59kg paneer, 11kg cream and 28kg ghee worth Rs 42,880.
Article Summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) seized 10,798.4kg of refined palmolein oil worth Rs 23,32,455 from a unit on Gangapur Road at Ghaygaon. The unit scored only 36 out of 86 marks (42%) and was declared Non-Compliant.
